intro: One scoop of stir-fried mixed vegetables is about 100 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories actually come from the stir-fry oil, not the vegetables.

variants.name: Mixed vegetables with prawns or squid

diet: Yes, and it should be on every plate. Vegetables give you fibre and fill up your plate, so you feel fuller for fewer calories. Even stir-fried, one scoop is still low in calories. Just pick ones that aren't too oily or swimming in thick starchy sauce.
tips: Take vegetables first and fill half your plate before adding other lauk.
Let the oily sauce drip off the scoop before putting it on your rice.
Cooking at home? Stir-fry with a little oil, then add a splash of water to steam in the pan.

swap.name: Blanched vegetables with a little oyster sauce
swap.why: Almost no oil, so you can take two scoops. More fibre and more filling.

faq.q: Do stir-fried vegetables still have nutrients?
faq.a: Yes, a quick stir-fry keeps a lot of the fibre and vitamins. Just don't overcook them until they're soggy.

faq.q: What vegetables are usually in sayur campur?
faq.a: Usually cabbage, carrot, long beans, mushrooms, baby corn and cauliflower. Some shops add fishballs or prawns.

faq.q: Why do shop vegetables always have thick sauce?
faq.a: Shops usually add cornflour or starch so the sauce sticks and looks glossy. It adds a few calories, so take the vegetables and leave most of the sauce.
